value: Amara-Nayaka territories were NOT hereditary and non-transferable; the king could transfer them
reasoning: The amara-nayaka system was a key political innovation of Vijayanagara: military commanders were given territories by the raya, collected taxes and kept part of the revenue for themselves and their troops. The kings occasionally transferred them from one place to another, so the claim that their territories were hereditary and non-transferable is incorrect.

The 102nd Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes. The 103rd (2019) introduced 10% EWS reservation. The 104th (2020) ended reserved seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, and the 106th (2023) provided one-third reservation for women.
